question: A finance manager is running a Cowork task that will reorganise files and send messages on her behalf. Which approach best matches sound practice for work that has real consequences?
options: A) Stay close and approve the actions that send or change things, reviewing what Claude does.
B) Let the task run without any pauses, then review the whole session once it has finished completely.
C) Approve every action once at the outset so the task is not interrupted while it is running.
D) Let the task run unattended overnight and check the results at the start of the next day.
correct_answers: A) Stay close and approve the actions that send or change things, reviewing what Claude does.
explanations: Correct. No approval setting replaces the person's judgment, and this task touches things with real consequences. Staying close and approving the sending and changing actions keeps her in control of exactly the steps that cannot be walked back.
Reviewing afterwards is fine for work that can be undone, but messages already sent in her name cannot be recalled. The review would document the damage rather than prevent it.
Blanket approval at the start grants permission for actions nobody has seen yet, which defeats the purpose of an approval step. Convenience is bought by removing the control the task most needs.
Running unattended overnight maximises the time between a mistake and its discovery. Recipients will have read the messages long before anyone looks at what happened.
